Connected charts

Source: vignettes/connected-charts.Rmd
connected-charts.Rmd

hc_connect() is a highcharter helper for linking separate widgets in an HTML document. Give the widgets the same group name, then choose the interactions each one shares with sync. Each widget keeps its own data, axes and legend. This also works for widgets rendered in separate Quarto HTML chunks on the same page; Shiny is not required.

Start with two time series

The built-in datasets::mdeaths and datasets::fdeaths series contain 72 months of deaths from bronchitis, emphysema and asthma in the United Kingdom, from 1974 to 1979. We will compare the monthly counts with their first differences.

The two line charts share tooltips, crosshairs and X zoom. Set hc_chart(zooming = list(type = "x")) to enable drag-to-zoom: including "zoom" in sync connects the ranges but does not enable the gesture itself.

men <- datasets::mdeaths
women <- datasets::fdeaths

first_difference <- function(x) {
  stats::ts(
    c(NA_real_, diff(as.numeric(x))),
    start = stats::start(x),
    frequency = stats::frequency(x)
  )
}

# Reuse explicit IDs and colors across the different views.
add_groups <- function(hc, men, women) {
  hc |>
    hc_add_series(
      data = men,
      id = "men",
      name = "Men",
      color = "#0072B2"
    ) |>
    hc_add_series(
      data = women,
      id = "women",
      name = "Women",
      color = "#D55E00"
    )
}

base <- highchart() |>
  hc_chart(type = "line", zooming = list(type = "x")) |>
  hc_xAxis(type = "datetime", crosshair = TRUE) |>
  hc_tooltip(shared = TRUE, table = TRUE, valueDecimals = 0) |>
  hc_plotOptions(
    series = list(
      animation = FALSE,
      marker = list(enabled = FALSE)
    )
  ) |>
  hc_legend(enabled = TRUE) |>
  hc_connect("lung-deaths", sync = c("hover", "zoom", "legend")) |>
  hc_size(height = 320)

levels <- base |>
  hc_title(text = "Monthly deaths from lung diseases") |>
  hc_subtitle(text = "United Kingdom, 1974-1979. Drag to zoom") |>
  hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Deaths")) |>
  add_groups(men, women)

changes <- base |>
  hc_title(text = "Change from the previous month") |>
  hc_yAxis(
    title = list(text = "Difference in deaths"),
    plotLines = list(list(value = 0, color = "#999999", width = 1))
  ) |>
  add_groups(first_difference(men), first_difference(women))

Hover matches points by their exact numeric X value, including timestamps. The leading NA preserves the first month in the difference series. That month has no difference to display, so hovering over it clears the other chart’s tooltip and crosshair. With category axes, use the same category order.

Add a pie and columns

Each chart has its own legend. Clicking a legend item toggles matching items in the other charts: series in the line and column charts, and individual points in the pie. The explicit id values establish these matches; names and colors alone do not connect them.

The two summary charts share only "legend". Their totals have no monthly X axis, so they do not participate in hover or zoom synchronization.

total_men <- sum(as.numeric(men))
total_women <- sum(as.numeric(women))

pie <- highchart() |>
  hc_chart(type = "pie") |>
  hc_title(text = "Share of all deaths") |>
  hc_subtitle(text = "Click a slice to select it") |>
  hc_add_series(
    name = "Deaths",
    data = list(
      list(id = "men", name = "Men", y = total_men, color = "#0072B2"),
      list(id = "women", name = "Women", y = total_women, color = "#D55E00")
    )
  ) |>
  hc_plotOptions(
    pie = list(
      showInLegend = TRUE,
      allowPointSelect = TRUE,
      cursor = "pointer",
      dataLabels = list(
        enabled = TRUE,
        format = "{point.name}: {point.percentage:.1f}%"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  hc_tooltip(valueDecimals = 0) |>
  hc_legend(enabled = TRUE) |>
  hc_connect("lung-deaths", sync = "legend") |>
  hc_size(height = 340)

columns <- highchart() |>
  hc_chart(type = "column") |>
  hc_title(text = "Total deaths") |>
  hc_subtitle(text = "Accumulated from 1974 to 1979") |>
  hc_xAxis(categories = "Entire period") |>
  hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Deaths"), min = 0) |>
  add_groups(total_men, total_women) |>
  hc_tooltip(shared = TRUE, table = TRUE, valueDecimals = 0) |>
  hc_legend(enabled = TRUE) |>
  hc_connect("lung-deaths", sync = "legend") |>
  hc_size(height = 340)

Selecting a pie slice with allowPointSelect = TRUE is a local interaction. hc_connect() synchronizes legend visibility, not point selection.

Arrange four connected charts

Place each line chart on its own row, followed by the pie and columns side by side: a 1 / 1 / 2 layout. The bottom row wraps on narrow screens. The layout uses htmltools; the connections come from the shared group, independently of where the widgets are placed on the page.

htmltools::tagList(
  levels,
  changes,
  htmltools::div(
    style = "display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px;",
    htmltools::div(
      style = "flex: 1 1 300px; min-width: 0;",
      pie
    ),
    htmltools::div(
      style = "flex: 1 1 300px; min-width: 0;",
      columns
    )
  )
)

Try these interactions in the charts above:

  • Hover over a month in either line chart to compare counts and changes.
  • Drag horizontally in either line chart to zoom both, then use either reset button to restore the full period.
  • Click Men or Women in any legend to hide or show that group in all four charts. The remaining pie slice fills the pie when the other group is hidden.
  • Click a pie slice to select it locally, without changing the other charts.
  • Narrow the browser window to stack the two summary charts.

For another independent set of charts on the same page, choose a different group name. See hc_connect() for the complete argument reference.
